svg.text: Figure 2-1 · Where the technical safety requirements sit
The 128 TSRs by block and by the element they are allocated to; 89 carry an ASIL. Status at the baseline: 21 implemented, 61 partly, 41 not, 5 assumed
QM, QM* (supports an ASIL TSR) or ext

"+": also allocated to another element. Status by the rule of WP-S-03 Figure 6-1, read from each TSR's implementation column; implemented means in the code at the baseline or the reference build, not verified.
Generated by fig_s02_allocation.py from trace/items/tsr.yaml, the copy of WP-S-02 §3–§10 and WP-S-06 that CI holds to the documents; nothing is hand-listed.

g.text: Terms: AoU assumption of use: what the analysis assumes about the car, the driver or the environment · ASIL Automotive Safety Integrity Level, A (lowest) to D (highest), from ISO 26262 · CI continuous integration:

the checks that run on every pull request · DM driver monitoring · E-nn element of the item (WP-C-01 §3.1), E-01…E-06 · EXT allocation to an existing vehicle element, credited only through an assumption of use

(WP-S-02 §2.2) · HAR allocation to the harness and relay (E-05; WP-S-02 §2.2) · HMI human-machine interface: display, sounds, cluster · MCU microcontroller: the panda safety processor (STM32H7) · OPS allocation to a

production or operation process (WP-S-02 §2.2) · P-HW allocation to the panda hardware: the safety MCU (E-04; WP-S-02 §2.2) · P-SW allocation to the panda firmware: the envelope on the safety MCU (E-03; WP-S-02

§2.2) · PCS pre-collision system: Toyota's stock collision warning and braking · QM quality managed: no ASIL; ordinary quality processes suffice · SoC system on chip: the comma device's main processor, running

openpilot (QM) · TSR-nn technical safety requirement (WP-S-02) · WP-nn work product, e.g. WP-C-04; the letter is its area (M management, C concept, S system, H hardware, W software, V validation, P processes, A
analyses, O operation, K safety case)
